        If their Week 5 performances are any indication of what's on tap on Sunday, the Steelers and Buccaneers' showdown might be one of the best on the Week 6 slate. After dropping their first four games, the Buccaneers stunned the Cowboys in front of a prime-time audience. Tampa Bay's 24-16 win was spearheaded by Bucky Irving (who ran for a career-high 165 yards) and a defense that forced three turnovers. The Steelers rebounded from a disheartening loss in Cleveland to post a double-digit win over the Colts last Sunday. The star of Pittsburgh's 34-22 win was running back Jaylen Warren, who became the first player since Herschel Walker (back in 1986) to have a 50-yard touchdown run and an 80-yard touchdown reception in the same game. Here's how you can follow the action, along with a breakdown and a prediction. Where to watch Steelers vs. Buccaneers liveWhen: Sunday, Oct. 18 | Time: 1 p.m. ETWhere: Raymond James Stadium -- Tampa, Florida TV: CBS | Stream: Paramount+ Follow:  CBS Sports AppOdds: Steelers -2.5, O/U 45.5 (via DraftKings Sportsbook)Daniels to get second start With Baker Mayfield still on the mend, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third career start. 
Daniels' first two starts were impressive. He completed over 70% of his passes in both games and showed impressive poise for a rookie. Against the Cowboys, Daniels completed a whopping 76% of his throws for 189 yards and a touchdown. He also took care of the ball after throwing two interceptions a week earlier against the Packers. He doesn't rely on his legs, but Daniels uses them as an asset nonetheless. He took off seven times against the Cowboys and had 55 yards on eight carries against the Packers. Unstoppable force vs. immovable object A key matchup will be Warren and the Steelers' running game against the Buccaneers' run defense. 
Warren, who is averaging 5.9 yards-per-carry and is Pittsburgh's leader in rushing and receiving, will face a Buccaneers defense that is second in the NFL in fewest rushing yards allowed (364), rushing touchdowns allowed (2) and average yards-per-carry allowed (3.3). It should be noted that the Buccaneers' defense has faced the sixth-fewest run plays in the NFL. Expect the Steelers to stay with the running game, even if it isn't bearing fruit early on. Next man up The Steelers will be without receivers Michael Pittman (foot), Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) for Sunday's game. Fellow wideout DK Metcalf has been tabbed as questionable with an illness that kept him from practicing on Friday. 
Last week, Pittsburgh's other pass catchers stepped up when Wilson and Skowronek exited early. Warren led the Steelers with 87 yards on six catches, rookie Germie Bernard set career-highs with six receptions and 80 yards, and tight end Pat Freiermuth caught two of Rodgers' three touchdown passes. Massive tight end Darnell Washington also caught two passes. Familiar face Pittsburgh will once again share a field with Danny Smith, a 32-year NFL coaching veteran who spent the previous 13 seasons as the Steelers' special teams coach. Smith joined Tampa Bay's coaching staff shortly after Mike Tomlin stepped down in January. Rest assured that Smith will look to exploit the weaknesses in Pittsburgh's special teams, which has not been one of the Steelers' strengths so far. The Steelers' kickoff returners are averaging just 22.7 yards per return (which is more than three yards under league average). Chris Boswell, a former Pro Bowler and one of the NFL's most reliable kickers over the past decade-plus, has already missed three field goals this season. 
The Steelers will have to overcome the absence of Skowronek, who was named to the Pro Bowl last season for his special-teams play. Prediction Pittsburgh feasted on rookie quarterbacks under Tomlin, and while he is no longer the Steelers' coach, expect new Steelers defensive play caller Patrick Graham to follow Tomlin's blueprint. The blueprint is pressure, which is the Steelers' calling card regardless of who the opposing quarterback is. Pittsburgh has unmatched depth at outside linebacker in T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith, Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer. Expect each of them to find their way into Tampa Bay's backfield on Sunday.  Score: Steelers 19, Buccaneers 13

title: How LeBron James, in his 24th season and first with the 76ers, can pass Michael Jordan in NBA GOAT debate - CBS Sports
description: LeBron is in search of his fifth title with a fourth different team as he starts a new journey in Philly
body:
LeBron is in search of his fifth title with a fourth different team as he starts a new journey in Philly
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:27 am ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Time is a thief that can rob you of youth before you realize it. That is the case for all of us ... except if your name is LeBron James. James, 41, is and is entering his 24th season in the NBA. When James' new team -- the 76ers -- plays its season opener on Tuesday night against the reigning champion Knicks at Madison Square Garden, it will be nearly 23 years to the day since James stepped on the floor in Sacramento to play in his first regular-season NBA game. I first wrote about James in the fall of 2003, when I was an 18-year-old high schooler in Ohio. As a college sophomore, I wrote about him again in 2006. Like many to come over the following years, the focus of that story was about whether James could one day surpass Michael Jordan, the sports icon of my childhood. And now here we are, two decades later. Like James, I am 41, a father and have been bitten by the golf bug. That's where comparisons between James and I end. But the comparisons between James and Jordan? As the past 20 years have shown us, they're not going anywhere.
James' unprecedented longevityLong ago, James answered the question as to whether or not he could live up to his unprecedented hype. He has, 10 times over. His laundry list of accomplishments includes four NBA titles (with three different franchises), four league MVPs, playing in an unfathomable eight straight Finals, being part of the NBA's first father-son duo, and being the catalyst behind the greatest comeback in NBA Finals history.From a longevity standpoint, James stands alone. He is the NBA's all-time leader in points and games played. He is the charter member of the 40K/10K/10K club (40,000 career points, 10,000 rebounds and 10,000 assists). 
Ironically, James' most famous play is not a basket, rebound or an assist. It's his block that helped end Cleveland's 52-year title drought. 
And he's still playing at a high level. He finished sixth in the MVP voting during his age-40 season. Last year, James led the Lakers to playoff series win after injuries sidelined Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves. James is ranked No. 19 on CBS Sports' list of the top 100 players entering the new season. The only NBA player who can remotely compare to James in terms of longevity is Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, who was still a quality starting center when he won his last two NBA titles at ages 40 and 41. Where the Jordan vs. LeBron debate stands nowThere is usually a generational divide when it comes to the James-Jordan debate. 
NBA fans who watched the Jordan era usually struggle to hand away the crown to James or to anyone else. We believe that we saw the greatest player who played the game at a level that had never been seen before and will never be seen again. Watching Jordan was just ... different. Otherworldly, even. Allen Iverson may have said it best during his Hall of Fame induction speech: "I remember the first time I played against him. I walked out on the court, I looked at him and for the first time in my life, a human being didn't look real to me." It's more than that, though. Jordan had more "moments" that any athlete in history. There's the 63-point game in Boston in '86, the slam dunk titles (back when that mattered), the game-winning shot in Cleveland in '89, the jaw-dropping layup in the '91 Finals, the 35-point first half points in the '92 Finals, the 55-point performance in the '93 Finals, his first championship after baseball and the tragic death of his father, the Flu Game, and my personal favorite, his 45-point performance in the '98 Finals that was punctuated by his title-clinching shot. 
Jordan wasn't just superhuman, so was his team, the Chicago Bulls, who ran the NBA for the majority of the '90s. No one knows this better than James, who was one of the millions of kids back then who grew up idolizing Jordan. To James' credit, he seems at peace with his legacy, both on and off the court, and he should. He doesn't need to prove anything to anyone. He really never did, but his drive to do so undoubtedly helped make him what he is today. Why a fifth title could push LeBron past MJFor the younger generations, James is their Jordan. But for those of us who remember Jordan and still refer to him as the GOAT, even we will have to concede that unofficial title to James if he -- at 42 years old -- wins a fifth title with a fourth franchise that hasn't won it all since 1983, the year before James' birth. 
James won't take solace in winning one playoff series in Philly. He said as much during the 76ers' media day. "I didn't leave my family to lose in the second round," he said. "I know that for sure."  It's a good thing James feels that way, because if he is going to definitively pass Jordan as the greatest of all-time, it'll take more than just winning a playoff series or two. It will take him and the 76ers winning it all. 
James would still be one championship behind Jordan, of course. But five championships with four different franchises, plus the unprecedented longevity, would make James' GOAT case as strong as it's ever been.The debates James and Jordan will likely never end, but the 2026-27 season gives James the best chance to add to his GOAT case that he's had in quite some time.

body:
Michigan and Penn State both enter Saturday's contest looking to snap losing streaks

        Big Ten rivals Penn State and Michigan will meet in the Big House Saturday in a matchup between two teams already in desperation mode midway through the season. Both began the 2026 season hopeful for the future with a new coach in charge. Six weeks into the season, that hope and optimism have turned into doom and gloom for both programs that enter Week 7 on losing streaks in Big Ten play. The Wolverines began the season with a controversial win before beating Oklahoma in Week 2 for what seemed, at the time, like Kyle Whittingham's first signature win in Ann Arbor. However, successive losses to Iowa and Minnesota, where the offense has looked inept, have raised the temperature under Whittingham just five games into his tenure. The Nittany Lions had a lengthy coaching search before finally bringing in Matt Campbell from Iowa State, and Penn State fans expected a swift return to Big Ten contention. Three consecutive losses to open conference play have already raised questions about Campbell's fit in State College, and he finds himself in desperation mode heading on the road into a hostile environment. 
For years, Penn State vs. Michigan was one of the biggest games of the year in the old Big Ten East. This year, what it lacks in intrigue regarding the College Football Playoff race, it makes up for in what it will tell us about the trajectory of two traditional Big Ten powers. The winner will be able to let out a sigh of relief, while the loser will be staring down a fight just to make it to a bowl game in 2026.   Michigan vs. Penn State: Need to know  Bryce Underwood as a runner: In Michigan's biggest win of the season against Oklahoma, it was Underwood running the ball that was the difference for the Wolverines. He carried the ball 18 times for 87 yards and one touchdown, which was by far his most productive rushing game of the season. The Penn State defense has struggled this season, and both Aidan Chiles and Colton Joseph have rushed for touchdowns against them for Northwestern and Wisconsin. Throwing the ball consistently hasn't been a strength of the Michigan offense, and in a game they desperately need, look for the Wolverines to try and take advantage of Underwood as a runner at times -- especially in red zone opportunities. Can Penn State create explosive plays?: Moving the ball on Michigan's defense consistently is a difficult task, and in both of their losses, it was explosives that led to scores for Minnesota and Iowa. Penn State's offense ranks in the middle of the pack in explosive plays this season, but has not been as dynamic since Koby Howard's injury took away their top downfield threat. If the Nittany Lions are going to score against Michigan, they have to find a way to produce some explosive plays. That doesn't always have to mean on offense. Iowa's first touchdown against Michigan came on a punt return. Minnesota forced three turnovers that led to 13 of their 20 points. Penn State will need a handful of chunk plays from the offense and to create some havoc on defense and special teams if they're going to win this game. 
Special teams, special teams, special teams: This is the kind of game where special teams matter a bit more than usual -- which is to say, this is going to be Big Ten football heritage on display. The punters on both sides need to be sharp and avoid handing the opponent a short field. With points at a premium, field goal opportunities will need to be converted. And with two offenses that can get stuck in the mud, a big return could swing this game one way or the other. Special teams has not been the strength of the Wolverines this season, as they rank 89th in special teams SP+, while Penn State is in the middle of the pack (49th).         The Philadelphia Eagles are not planning to place quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is out this week with a superficial blood clot, on injured reserve, according to ESPN. The team has reportedly not even discussed the possibility of IR for their QB. Going on IR sidelines a player for at least four weeks.The Eagles released a statement saying Hurts requested treatment on his calf four days after their Week 4 loss against the Los Angeles Rams. The Eagles performed an ultrasound on his leg after they landed in London for their game against the Jacksonville Jaguars and found the superficial blood clot. The team's medical staff determined he could play, and the team conducted a follow-up ultrasound where they found the blood clot had moved, which can lead to a serious health situation. When he can play will be determined by his medical team. Hurts is still working on the best treatment plan for the situation and the team believes it is treatable. Hurts and the team are both still looking into more options and are putting the quarterback's health as top priority. 
If the medical team believes IR is the best path for Hurts, he could still end up on it. Blood thinners are a main treatment for blood clots and a player cannot play while on that medication. Typically, a patient would be on blood thinners for six weeks, but if the clot is minor, it may be treatable with other measures, such as anti-inflammatories. If the clot worsens, it could mean more time on blood thinners, which would, in turn, mean more time away from the field. With Hurts out this week against the Carolina Panthers, Tanner McKee will be leading the offense, and rookie Cole Payton will be the backup. 
The Eagles added some security in the quarterback position this week, signing Joe Milton off the Dallas Cowboys practice squad. They now have four QBs, a number that led some to believe Hurts was headed to IR.

The 2026 WNBA Finals tip off on Saturday afternoon ... so who will capture the championship?

        The WNBA will have a first-time champion in 2026. The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream are squaring off in the 2026 WNBA Finals, and neither franchise has ever won a title. The Valkyries are in just their second season after debuting as an expansion team in 2025. The Dream, meanwhile, have been to the WNBA Finals on three occasions (2010, 2011 and 2013) but have been swept each time.They both knocked out more-experienced teams to get here. The Valkyries took down the reigning champion Aces in the semis, while the Dream ousted the Liberty. So who will win a historic title in 2026? Before Game 1 on Saturday, our experts are making their predictions.2026 WNBA Finals predictions
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Lindsay Gibbs
                            
            
                    
    
                                            
                    
                                    Jack Maloney
                            
            2026 WNBA Finals pick
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Dream
                    
    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
        
                            Valkyries
                    
    
    Expert explanationsGibbs: Dream in 7. The Golden State Valkyries won the regular-season series over the Atlanta Dream 3-0, but that record doesn't quite tell the whole story. Two of those games were decided in the final minute, and all three of those meetings came in a 10-day span early in the season, with the Valkyries getting wins over the Dream on June 24, June 26 and July 4.
Those three losses were part of a five-game losing skid by the Dream, who sat at 12-9 on July 5.The Dream have only lost five games total since, finishing the regular season with an 18-5 run. Including the postseason, Atlanta has won 10 in a row and 14 of its last 15. In August and September, the Dream led the league in offense with a 115.2 rating and were second only to the Valkyries with a 100.8 defensive rating, both about five-point improvements on their early-season ratings. Simply put, this is a different Dream team than the one the Valkyries swept this summer.I can truly talk myself into either team winning this series – both are obviously in exceptional form and have been for the past three months, both feel like teams of destiny, both are trying to win the first title for their franchise and both are physical, dogged competitors who aren't afraid of winning ugly, which is a requirement for every title team.
The Valkyries are healthier and deeper than the Dream – the Allisha Gray injury is a big worry for Atlanta – and have home-court advantage. Defense wins championships, and the Valkyries have been far and away the best defense all season. And yet, I'm giving the Dream the edge. They have two players who have won WNBA titles in DeWanna Bonner and Jordin Canada, the far more potent offense and, while the Valkyries have the best defense, the Dream have the edge on the boards and in the paint.In the spirit of Angel Reese and Joe Lacob, I am manifesting an epic seven-game series full of twists and turns. And, at the end, it will be a big defensive play by Reese that will seal the title for the Dream on the road in front of a raucous Ballhalla crowd on Halloween night.
        
            
                From stunning Angel Reese trade to expansion ingenuity: How Dream, Valkyries broke the mold to reach Finals
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Maloney: Valkyries in 6. I wish that we had more clarity on Allisha Gray's injury, what procedure she had done and what she'll be able to give the Dream -- if she's even able to play at all. Both teams have similar styles and it's difficult to get a good feel on this matchup in the best of circumstances. The uncertainty surrounding Gray makes it nearly impossible.
It is safe to assume Gray will not be close to 100% if she does play, however, especially early in the series, and that's one of the reasons I'm going with the Valkyries. Gray led the Dream in scoring during the regular season at 19 points per game, which was good for ninth in the league, and was their go-to option late in games. Jordin Canada, DeWanna Bonner and Isobel Borlase were able to make up for Gray's production in the semifinals, but I'm not super confident they can continue to hit such incredible heights, especially against the best defense in the league.I'm going to crib here from an article I wrote about Gray's injury, which shows how incredible that trio was last round:Canada had three of the five-highest playoff scoring performances of her career against the Liberty, and averaged 22.3 points on 62.2/61.5/100 shooting splits -- up from 11.6 points on 43.1/29.2/78.2 shooting in the regular season. Bonner went for 15.3 points and 8.3 rebounds on 50/46.7/80 shooting splits, up from 10.4 points and six rebounds on 40.2/27.9/84.3 shooting between the Phoenix Mercury and Dream in the regular season. And Borlase, who only had six double-digit scoring games in the regular season, came off the bench to chip in 11 points in Game 2 and 10 points in Game 3 while shooting 9 of 15, including 3 of 6 from 3-point range. Of course, the counterpoint there is they may not have to be that good if Gray is back and Rhyne Howard doesn't shoot 31.1% from the field like she did against the Liberty. Regardless, I worry about the Dream's ability to generate consistent offense, especially with how reliant they are on forcing turnovers, and how good the Valkyries are at taking care of the ball. During the regular season, the Dream led the league in opponent turnover rate (19.5%) and points off turnovers (18.1), but the Valkyries were tied for second in turnover rate (15.1%) and first in opponent points off turnovers (11.7) by a wide margin.The Valkyries have plenty of their own offensive issues and regardless of Gray's status will have trouble scoring against a Dream defense that has been spectacular in the playoffs. Time and time and time again, however, the Valkyries have made it clear that they're not only capable of winning ugly, they prefer it that way.I also think the Valkyries' homecourt advantage will be a big factor in this series. The Valkyries were a league-best 17-5 at home during the regular season, and are 4-0 at Chase Center during the playoffs. Their defense, which was four points per 100 possessions than any other team this season, was even better at home, where they boasted a 98.2 defensive rating and a 19.7% opponent turnover rate. Ballhalla is the most raucous atmosphere in the league, and can cause opponents to spiral, as we've already seen this postseason. Plus, the Valkyries shot 36.1% from 3-point range at home, compared to 32.6% on the road. For a team that once again broke the record by taking 30.3 3s per game, that's a big deal.All told, I'm going Valkyries in 6 in what should be an extremely tough, physical and competitive series.

The No. 5 Hoosiers play host to the fourth-ranked Buckeyes with their undefeated record on the line. The winner will have the inside track to the Big Ten Championshiop Game in Indianapolis The reigning national champion, Indiana, hasn't faced a single ranked team, and it's had one of the easier schedules in the Big Ten. The Hoosiers did get a dicey road test against Nebraska last weekend, but that was a nice warm-up for what's to come on Saturday. Despite losing a number of key pieces from last year's team, Indiana still looks like a serious title contender thanks to newcomers Nick Marsh (528 receiving yards and six touchdowns), Turbo Richard (leads Big Ten in rushing yards) and Tobi Osunsanmi (leads the Big Ten in sacks and tackles for loss).Ohio State will be looking for a little revenge after losing to Indiana in the 2025 Big Ten Championship. That loss snapped the Buckeyes' 30-game winning streak over the Hoosiers, so they'll try to start a new one on Saturday. That's entirely possible, largely due to the presence of Heisman Trophy favorite and athletic anomaly Jeremiah Smith, who leads the conference in just about every major receiving category.This is one of the best games on a loaded Week 7 slate, so here is everything you must know as No. 5 Indiana visits No. 4 Ohio State.

When the game kicks off Saturday, it will be the third time in as many years that Indiana and Ohio State have played with both teams ranked inside the top five. If we're honest, Indiana was the main reason there were no top-five matchups in the first 97 meetings, but that has changed in a big way now. The Hoosiers have the resources and the coach to compete with the Buckeyes, so we may have a budding Big Ten rivalry on our hands.Smith's historic season: Every week, Smith rewrites the record books at the program, conference and NCAA level. That could continue on Saturday because Smith is just one receiving touchdown shy of matching Michigan legend Braylon Edwards for the most in Big Ten history (39). Smith has already secured the school records for career receptions (211), receiving yards (3,474) and receiving touchdowns (38). He should only add to those totals against a Hoosiers secondary Smith beat for 144 yards last year.

Osunsanmi and Stephen Daley have combined for 10 sacks, and Ohio State has allowed 11 sacks of Sayin thus far. The battle between the Indiana defensive front and the Ohio State offensive line in pass protection will be critical.Ohio State vs. Indiana prediction, picks  This should be another tremendous game between a pair of national title contenders, and it may very well be a preview of the Big Ten Championship matchup. Having said that, I do wonder how well Indiana's passing defense will hold up for 60 minutes, especially without D'Angelo Ponds in the secondary this time. title: Joel Embiid explains why he's 'against the concept of sacrificing' for the star-studded 76ers - CBS Sports
description: Embiid doesn't think any of the Sixers stars need to take a back seat this season
body:
Embiid doesn't think any of the Sixers stars need to take a back seat this season
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Oct 17, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:40 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia 76ers are the latest NBA organization to build a superteam, adding Jaylen Brown and LeBron James this offseason to create a starting lineup with four All-Stars alongside Tyrese Maxey and Joel Embiid. James. in particular, knows exactly what it takes to get a team of stars to accomplish their ultimate goal of winning a championship, but this 76ers squad is approaching things a little bit differently than James' Big 3 Heat. Where Chris Bosh was the player to clearly sacrifice his role for the betterment of the team alongside James and Dwyane Wade in Miami, Embiid said after Friday's preseason finale that he believes the Sixers can thrive without needing anyone to take a back seat to anyone else, via ESPN. "I'm against the concept of sacrificing," Embiid said. "I think the way I explained it was you do what you do best, and we're going to support you. ... I don't think anybody has to take a back seat."
The Sixers can certainly structure their rotations to where each of their four stars has moments throughout a game where they get to be the focal point. However, when all four share the court together, there will need to be a hierarchy in place, particularly come crunch time in close games. That's going to require some give-and-take from the four stars, and it could be dependent on their opponent as to which of their stars has the biggest advantage. Embiid may prefer to call it support rather than sacrifice or a back seat, but the Sixers are going to have to learn how to work together and play secondary roles to make this all work. What may help the Sixers the most is that no one understands that more than James, and the 42-year-old taking a minimum to sign in Philly signaled he's happy to play that supporting role and pitch in as a lead option when needed. 
Jaylen Brown also has experience playing off a fellow star and winning a championship, so there shouldn't be any shortage of understanding of what it takes to succeed. The bigger question is whether everyone can come to an agreement on how that works best, making Nick Nurse's biggest task ego management Sixers bolster center depth in a (literal) big wayWhile Embiid and the Sixers stars figure out how they can all maximize each other's strengths, the organization is still trying to piece together a center rotation behind Embiid. After Ariel Hukporti suffered a season-ending Achilles injury, Philadelphia found itself extremely thin at the five behind Embiid, with Adem Bona -- who has missed the preseason with a foot sprain -- as the only reserve center on the roster. On Saturday, the Sixers addressed their issues in the short term by converting Tacko Fall to a two-way contract after having him signed to a camp deal. The 7-foot-6 big man has missed the preseason with a hip strain, but the Sixers must feel confident he'll be able to help them fairly soon to bolster their rotation. 
Fall has been out of the NBA since the 2021-22 season when he played 11 games with the Cavaliers. In his career he's only played in 37 games in three seasons, but the Sixers must believe he can be a contributor to their rotation to convert him into a two-way spot. With their first apron hard cap, Philadelphia couldn't even add a vet minimum full-season deal after Hukporti went down, and Fall could be a relatively short-term stopgap until their cap situation allows for a partial-season deal. Between stars learning how to work together and Nurse trying to cobble together a center rotation behind Embiid, there will be no shortage of intrigue in Philly at the start of the season.

        In May, Daniel Dubois won the WBO heavyweight championship with a stoppage win over Fabio Wardley. On Saturday, the pair will run it back in London (2 p.m. ET, DAZN PPV). That rematch highlights boxing's weekend schedule, though it's not the only world title fight on the menu.In the first meeting between Dubois and Wardley, Wardley scored knockdowns of Dubois in the first and third rounds. Despite that early success, the real story of the fight was the toughness Wardley showed across the rest of the fight, absorbing a tremendous beating from Dubois.Dubois was able to take advantage of Wardley's limited offensive approach and land crushing right hands round after round. All Wardley could do in response was go back to the well with the same looping one-two combinations that had produced the earlier knockdowns.
Wardley started boxing late in life, competing in white-collar shows from age 21 before turning professional. He found plenty of success, including late comeback knockout wins over Justis Huni and Joseph Parker in interim title fights before being promoted to full champion ahead of the Dubois fight.
Dubois came up in a more traditional fashion, working through the amateurs before turning pro. That seasoning provided the skills and knowledge that allowed Dubois to make further adjustments and become a more dynamic fighter after he tasted Wardley's power early on."I enjoy inflicting pain and putting that chaos on the other guy, what's inside me, and the pain, you know, I put it on him," Dubois said this week. "That's how boxing is, it releases your, whatever you have inside you, it's an outlet, isn't it? So, yeah, I'm looking forward to it."Dubois has three losses in his career, all by knockout, including a pair to Oleksandr Usyk. Beyond those losses, Dubois has picked up many big wins, including over Anthony Joshua in a British megafight in 2024.
Prediction: There's no reason to think the rematch plays out much differently than the first bout. That is especially true with the rematch coming so shortly after the first meeting. As mentioned, Wardley took a hellacious beating in that fight, and since then he has had to recover as much as possible and hasn't had much time to add new wrinkles to his game. Dubois is the better fighter, and as long as he can avoid a pure knockout shot, he should be able to put a hurting on Wardley again. Pick: Daniel Dubois via TKO7Sebastian Fundora vs. Ermal HadribeajThe other big fight on Saturday takes place in Las Vegas, where Sebastian Fundora will defend his WBC junior middleweight title against Ermal Hadribeaj (8 p.m. ET, DAZN).Fundora has developed into a really good fighter after starting his career seen by many as a sideshow, with his 6-foot-6 frame towering over opponents, but a tendency to fight toe-to-toe rather than at a range that best utilized his reach. As things seemed to have been moving in the right direction, Fundora suffered a shocking knockout loss to Brian Mendoza.
Fundora rebounded from the Mendoza loss with a split-decision win over Tim Tszyu that was largely attributed to Tszyu suffering a nasty cut early in the fight as a result of a Fundora elbow. Fundora erased all doubt about that win two fights later, stopping Tszyu just seven rounds into the fight.In his most recent fight, Fundora took just six rounds to stop Keith Thurman in their March bout.Hadribeaj isn't a big-name fighter, and Fundora is far and away the best opponent he will have faced, but at 23-0-1, Hadribeaj has yet to suffer a loss. His most recent fight was a career-best win, taking a decision win over previously undefeated Bakary Samake.
That said, Hadribeaj has only scored eight knockouts in his career, so he likely doesn't have the power to keep Fundora off of him as the fight wears on.Prediction: This is set up to be little more than a showcase for Fundora. He has the better resume and the kind of physical tools that simply can't be taught. Now that Fundora better mixes in fighting at distance with his ability to stand and trade inside, he's a very big problem for the junior middleweight division. Hadribeaj doesn't figure to be the fighter who can take the belt from Fundora's waist. Pick: Sebastian Fundora via TKO4
